content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Happy to help you build a bookmark manager. Before I start scaffolding anything, I want to make sure I build the right thing. A few quick questions:

## 1. Platform & form factor
- **Web app** (runs in a browser, accessible anywhere)?
- **CLI tool** (terminal-based, fast for power users)?
- **Desktop app** (Electron/native)?
- **Browser extension** (save the current tab with one click)?

## 2. Core features — which of these do you want?
- Add / edit / delete bookmarks (URL, title, notes)
- **Tags or folders** for organization
- **Search / filter**
- **Auto-fetch** page title & favicon from the URL
- Import/export (e.g. from browser bookmarks HTML)
- Multi-user / accounts, or just **you** (single user, local)?

## 3. Where does data live?
- Local file (SQLite / JSON) — simplest, private, no server
- Hosted database — needed if you want to access from multiple devices

## 4. Tech preferences
Any stack you want (or want to avoid)? If you have no preference, my default recommendation for something clean and low-maintenance would be:

> **A local web app**: Python (FastAPI) or Node backend + SQLite, with a simple HTML/JS frontend. Runs on your machine, no cloud needed, easy to extend later.

---

If you'd rather I just **pick sensible defaults and start building**, tell me and I'll go with the recommendation above (single-user, local, tags + search + auto-title). What sounds right to you?
Just pick sensible defaults and start building — the recommendation you described sounds good to me. Local web app, single user, with tags and search and the auto-title thing. Go for it.

content:
Done. Your bookmark manager is built and tested end-to-end.

## What you've got

A local, single-user web app — **FastAPI + SQLite backend**, **vanilla HTML/JS/CSS frontend** (no build step). Data lives in one `bookmarks.db` file on your machine.

```
/work
├── app/
│   ├── main.py       # API routes
│   ├── db.py         # SQLite schema + helpers
│   ├── titles.py     # auto-fetch page titles
│   └── static/       # index.html, app.js, style.css
├── requirements.txt
├── run.sh            # one-command launcher (sets up venv on first run)
└── README.md
```

## How to run it

```bash
cd /work && ./run.sh
```

Then open **http://127.0.0.1:8000**. (The venv and deps are already installed, so it starts immediately.)

## Features, all verified working

- **Add / edit / delete** bookmarks with URL, title, and notes
- **Auto-title** — leave the title blank and it's fetched from the page (confirmed: `example.com` → "Example Domain")
- **Tags** — comma-separated, deduped, case-insensitive; click a tag (in the sidebar or on a card) to filter
- **Search** — matches URL, title, and notes as you type
- Editing a bookmark cleanly re-syncs its tags; deletes cascade

I smoke-tested every endpoint (create, list, search, tag-filter, update, delete, 404s, title preview) and cleared the test data so you start with an empty database. Interactive API docs are at `/docs` when the server's running.

## A few notes on choices I made
- **No `pip` was on the system**, so `run.sh` bootstraps its own venv via `ensurepip` — the app stays self-contained.
- Title fetching is **best-effort**: network errors or timeouts just leave the title blank rather than failing the save.
- URLs without a scheme get `https://` prepended automatically.

Want me to add any of these next? **Import from browser bookmarks (HTML export)**, **favicons**, **export/backup button**, or a **"save current tab" bookmarklet**.
